18                THE SECRETARY:   Legislative 

19   Resolution Number 3550, by Senator Ritchie, 

20   memorializing Governor Andrew M. Cuomo to 

21   proclaim February 2, 2016, as Canada-Quebec- 

22   Ontario Day in the State of New York.  

23                "WHEREAS, Canada is New York's  

24   primary export market, with $34.2 billion worth 

25   of merchandise goods exchanged and 17 percent of 


                                                                401

 1   New York's worldwide exports sold to Canada in 

 2   2014; in addition, 680,900 New York jobs are 

 3   supported by Canada-U.S. trade; and 

 4                "WHEREAS, New York and Canada share 

 5   an international border measuring 445 miles in 

 6   length with 17 international border crossings, 

 7   featuring several important international trade 

 8   corridors including the Quebec-New York Corridor, 

 9   the Capitol Corridor, and Continental One, as 

10   well as the second-busiest crossing between 

11   Canada and the United States at the Peace Bridge; 

12   and 

13                "WHEREAS, The New York-Canada 

14   partnership boasts the largest bilateral tourism 

15   industry in the United States, with over 

16   6.9 million Canadians visiting New  York, 

17   accounting for over $1.7 billion in expenditures 

18   in 2012; and 

19                "WHEREAS, Reflective of this strong 

20   security relationship, the Eastern Air Defense 

21   Sector, headquartered in Rome, New York, is 

22   staffed by active-duty New York Air National 

23   Guardsmen and a Canadian Forces Detachment; this 

24   unit supports NORAD's integrated warning and 

25   attach assessment mission and the U.S. Northern  


                                                                402

 1   Command's homeland defense mission; and 

 2                "WHEREAS, Over 19 million 

 3   New Yorkers depend on Canada and its vast energy 

 4   reserves to fuel our state, importing over 

 5   $4.7 billion worth of energy from Canada in 2014; 

 6   and 

 7                "WHEREAS, Quebec more specifically 

 8   has been an important supplier of clean, 

 9   renewable energy to New York for decades; and 

10                "WHEREAS, New York is the primary 

11   international market for Quebec, with the total 

12   value of bilateral trade amounting to 

13   $7.4 billion in 2014; and exports to New York 

14   represent 11.5 percent of Quebec's U.S.-bound  

15   exports, with an emphasis on unwrought aluminum, 

16   petroleum products, refined copper and 

17   hydroelectricity; and 

18                "WHEREAS, Quebec established its 

19   first office abroad in 1940 in New York City, and 

20   has maintained this important commercial, 

21   investment, educational and cultural link to 

22   New York and neighboring states for 75 years; and 

23                "WHEREAS, Financial ties between 

24   Quebec and New York go back almost a century and 

25   a half, when Quebec became the first foreign 


                                                                403

 1   issuer of bonds on Wall Street in 1879; and 

 2                "WHEREAS, Ontario and New York are 

 3   closely linked geographically, both bordering on 

 4   Lake Erie and Lake Ontario and having border  

 5   crossing points in the Niagara and St. Lawrence 

 6   regions; and the jurisdictions have in common a 

 7   significant number of economic, social,  

 8   environmental, educational and cultural interests 

 9   and connections; and 

10                "WHEREAS, More than 63 percent of 

11   Canada's total bilateral trade with New York -- 

12   over $24 billion -- was between Ontario and 

13   New York, with Ontario's primary exports to 

14   New York including unwrought gold and silver,  

15   engines, autos and electrical energy, and 

16   Ontario's primary imports from New York including 

17   petroleum gases, metals, motor vehicle parts and 

18   engines; and 

19                "WHEREAS, The economies of Ontario 

20   and New York are tightly linked through 

21   integrated cross-border supply chains that keep 

22   our firms competitive, including, for example, 

23   auto parts that cross the border sometimes 

24   several times before completion; and 

25                "WHEREAS, Canada -- and in 


                                                                404

 1   particular its provinces of Quebec and Ontario -- 

 2   and New York share many more deep economic, 

 3   historical, cultural and familial ties as well; 

 4   now, therefore, be it 

 5                "RESOLVED, That this Legislative 

 6   Body pause in its deliberations to memorialize  

 7   Governor Andrew M. Cuomo to proclaim February 2, 

 8   2016 as Canada-Quebec-Ontario Day in the State of 

 9   New York; and be it further 

10                "RESOLVED, That copies of this  

11   resolution, suitably engrossed, be transmitted to  

12   the Honorable Andrew M. Cuomo, Governor of the 

13   State of New York; the Consulate General of 

14   Canada in New York; the Quebec Government Office 

15   in New York; and the Office of the Ontario 

16   Government Representative in Washington, D.C."

20   Mr. President.

22   to welcome representatives of the Canadian, 

23   Ontario and Quebec governments to our chambers 

24   today.  

25                I'd like to take a moment just to 


                                                                405

 1   recognize a few:  Mr. John Prato, Consul General 

 2   of Canada in New York; Mr. Jean-Claude Lauzon, 

 3   Delegate General of the Quebec Government in 

 4   New York; and Ms. Monique Smith, Ontario 

 5   Provincial Representative to the United States.  

 6                I want to welcome you all today.  I 

 7   know many of my colleagues are always surprised 

 8   when they find out that it takes me about 

 9   four and a half hours to get to the capital of 

10   New York where I work, but I can get to the 

11   nation's capital in Canada in less than an hour.  

12   So I think people are really kind of amazed at 

13   that.

14                And I know living and growing up so 

15   close to the border, I think it's given me a 

16   different perspective.  I know when my kids were 

17   playing hockey when they were young, if our local 

18   arena was full and we didn't want to drive 

19   20 miles to the next community in New York, we 

20   would think nothing of jumping in the car and 

21   going to practice a couple of miles over the 

22   border in Canada.  

23                And so I've always been keenly aware 

24   of just the wonderful honor it is to be able to 

25   live and share the relationship with the 


                                                                406

 1   Canadians across the broader.

 2                Because of that, you know, I've been 

 3   able to kind of keep track of the traffic, the 

 4   Canadian plates on the road, but I'm even more 

 5   keenly aware of it now as the Senator who 

 6   represents 175 miles of border along the 

 7   St. Lawrence River and Ontario.  And so the 

 8   economics between the Canadians and the 

 9   New Yorkers, especially in my district, is 

10   something that's extremely important to our local 

11   economy, but it's extremely important to New York 

12   as a whole, as Canada is our number-one trading 

13   partner.

15   coming here today, for sending your message and 

16   letting us all know how important our 

17   relationship is.  And I certainly appreciate the 

18   friendship we've had for hundreds of years 

19   between the Canadians and New Yorkers, and look

22   invitation to my colleagues to come to my 

23   district and we'll take a couple of minutes just

 1   also.

 1   Canadian border that borders both the provinces 

 2   of Quebec and Ontario.  And we have had a great 

 3   relationship.  I think I have met the

 9   something that someone said that is far more 

10   eloquent than something that I could say.  In May 

11   of 1961, before a session of Parliament, 

12   then-President John Kennedy said that "Geography 

13   has made us neighbors, history has made us 

14   friends.  Economics has made us partners, 

15   necessity has made us allies.  Those whom nature 

16   hath has so joined together, let no man put 

17   asunder."

18                Merci, mes amis.  God bless Canada

 1                Let me first start by welcoming the 

 2   consul general, John Prato, here to the Senate 

 3   chambers here in the Empire State of New York.  

 4   Also the delegate general of Quebec, the 

 5   provincial representative of Ontario, welcome.  

 6                I also want to recognize somebody 

 7   who has played an instrumental role in my life, 

 8   is now playing an instrumental role in the 

 9   consul general's life, and that's senior 

10   diplomatic advisor Rachel Homewood, who's my 

11   former legislative director.  She's here with the 

12   consul general.

15   I'd like to say that I taught her a thing or two,

20   this resolution and thank the sponsor of this 

21   resolution for bringing this to our attention 

22   today.  You know, it's important that we 

23   celebrate these victories, and this is a victory 

24   between our two countries -- 150 years, going on 

25   150 years next year, the sesquicentennial, the 


                                                                410

 1   150th birthday of Canada.  And in those 

 2   150 years, New York State specifically, but of 

 3   course both of our nations in our entireties, 

 4   have tremendous relationships that we can share 

 5   with the rest of the world, an amazing 

 6   demonstration of peace between our two nations.

 7                The fabric of our communities, the 

 8   fabric of our nations is reflected in that peace:  

 9   the culture, the sports and, yes, the economy.  

10   And the mutual relationship that we have and the 

11   mutual benefit that we have between New York 

12   State and the United States, and Canada, 

13   particularly Quebec and Ontario.  And the 

14   economies that we share, the individuals that 

15   pour over the borders in each direction to 

16   celebrate each other's communities, respectively.  

17   It's an incredible collaboration that we need to 

18   not only celebrate, but it is our duty to 

19   enhance.

20                And Consul General, I was there with 

21   you yesterday, listening intently on the 

22   importance of growing our economies between the 

23   United States and Canada.  And as we make 

24   decisions here in New York State, as 

25   decisions are made down in Washington, it is 


                                                                411

 1   extremely vital that we take into consideration 

 2   the historic nature that the Canadian economy has 

 3   played in our country and in our state and 

 4   continue to deliver on that relationship.

 5                So I am thrilled to have you here 

 6   today.  An early happy birthday to your great 

 7   country.  And I look forward to furthering and 

 8   fostering our relationship well into the future.  

 9                Welcome.

11   Kennedy, thank you.

14   Mr. President.

15                It's an honor for me to join my 

16   colleagues in welcoming our wonderful friends 

17   from Canada, particularly from Quebec and 

18   Ontario.  They are truly not only our partners, 

19   but they are our friends, and we work very 

20   closely together.

21                My district is -- some people ask me 

22   what does it involve and where is it.  I tell 

23   them it's from Cambridge, New York, to Canada.  

24   Clinton and Franklin County have a border with 

25   Canada, as does St. Lawrence County.  


                                                                412

 1                And you would be surprised, I am 

 2   sure, at the figure that in Clinton County, every 

 3   morning 15 percent of the population gets up and 

 4   goes to work at a Canadian company.

 5                We have such a great partnership and 

 6   such a great relationship that our economy 

 7   depends upon Canada, and how well they do is how 

 8   well my area does.  Many of the products of 

 9   Canadian companies that are made in my district, 

10   you use.  Bombardier makes subway cars, 

11   Metro-North, all of that.  Nova Bus providing 

12   buses to New York City.  And down in the southern 

13   part of my district, I have Irving Tissue from 

14   New Brunswick, and they make all of the Wegmans 

15   paper towel products and many of our 

16   private-label products.

17                So you're an important partner.  And 

18   we talk about buying, we want to buy North 

19   American, so that Canada is included in us when 

20   we talk about our economy, our manufacturing, and 

21   how important they are to us.

22                So thank you for being here, and 

23   thanks for being such great partners with us.  

24                Thank you.
